item.title: ACAMB advises bank customers against phishing scams
item.description: The Association of Corporate Communication and Marketing Professionals in Banks (ACAMB) has urged bank customers to remain vigilant against phishing scams and other forms of cyber fraud, warning that criminals are increasingly using fake bank alerts, cloned websites and impersonation accounts to steal sensitive financial information. The warning follows a fraudulent text message impersonating various banks. FactCheckAfrica debunked the message, finding that the link it contained led to a cloned internet banking website designed to steal customers’ login credentials, BVNs, card details and transaction PINs. The incident highlights the risks associated with digital banking fraud in Nigeria. In June, Wema Bank suspended its engagements on X, (formerly known as Twitter) amid reports of more than 70 fake accounts impersonating the bank and its ALAT platform. In August, Zenith Bank Plc disclosed that it was investigating unauthorised access to customer data linked to a global cyberattack. ACAMB President, Jide Sipe, warned that fraudsters were increasingly adopting sophisticated methods to impersonate trusted banking brands and steal customers’ personal information, making their schemes difficult to distinguish from legitimate communications. “When a scam message carries your name, your phone number or your bank’s logo, it looks real. That is exactly why customers must slow down. No bank in Nigeria will ask you to confirm your PIN, password, OTP or BVN through a link,” Sipe said. Sipe acknowledged the efforts of banks to strengthen fraud detection and customer protection, alongside regulatory measures introduced by the Central Bank of Nigeria’s mandatory cybersecurity self assessment guide. He stressed, however, that these efforts must be complemented by customer awareness and vigilance, particularly when handling requests for sensitive banking information. “Banks can strengthen their security systems, but fraudsters continue to find ways to exploit unsuspecting customers. We must all remain vigilant. Always pause, verify requests through official channels and report anything suspicious before taking action,” he added. Sipe urged customers to avoid clicking links in unsolicited messages asking them to verify, reactivate or secure their bank accounts. He also warned against sharing personal identification numbers (PINs), passwords, one-time passwords (OTPs), card verification values (CVVs) or BVNs in response to suspicious requests. Customers should verify such requests directly with their banks through official mobile applications, verified social media accounts or published customer service numbers. item.title: World Ports Confab: FG woos global investors with maritime reforms
item.description: By Godwin Oritse The Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA) has intensified efforts to attract global investment into Nigeria’s maritime sector by showcasing the Federal Government’s ongoing port reforms and investor-friendly policies at the World Ports Conference, highlighting opportunities for private sector participation, improved port efficiency and sustainable growth. Speaking at the ongoing World Ports Conference in London, Managing Director of the Nigerian Ports Authority, Dr Abubakar Dantsoho, showcased President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s maritime policies and its positioning of Nigeria’s Ports as Africa’s biggest economy that is yearning for global investment. He affirmed that the speed of growth and development in the country’s ports signifies the huge opportunities investors should tap into, adding that the current administration of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has put policies in place that are investment friendly. The NPA boss identified Nigeria’s huge population, urbanization, and infrastructural gaps in the ports as attractive opportunities for investment in its maritime and associated sectors. Dantsoho, who is also the Vice- President of the International Association of Ports & Harbours (IAPH) and doubles as Chairman of the Port Management Association of West and Central Africa (PMAWCA) told investors that Africa’s untapped resources remain the best destination for ports investment and development. He said the government alone cannot fund development of bigger or deeper sea ports and other similar projects hence the need for investors to take advantage of such opportunities across the continent. Dantsoho affirmed that “Nigeria has the highest population in Africa. So, the speed of growth is something that really should concern us. For example, in Nigeria, only recently, about 3 years ago, we commissioned the first deep sea port in Nigeria, which is called Lekki Deep Sea Port, that was funded by the Chinese government in relationship with China Harbor, and the expenditure cost us $1.6 billion to build Lekki in Lagos. The post World Ports Confab: FG woos global investors with maritime reforms appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: BoI advocates investment in industrial clusters to boost Lagos economy
item.description: By Babajide Komolafe The Bank of Industry (BOI) has called for increased investment in industrial clusters, reliable power supply and supporting infrastructure to boost productivity, attract private capital and strengthen the Lagos State economy. Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer, BoI, Dr. Olasupo Olusi made this call in a keynote address delivered at the 4th edition of the Lagos Economic Outlook 2027 Discourse, themed, ‘“Development Pathways, Emerging Risks and Strategic Policy Priorities.’ Represented by Dr. Isa Omagu, General Manager, MD/CEO’s Office, BoI, Olusi said investment in industrial clusters, particularly along major industrial and port corridors, would help businesses overcome production constraints, reduce operating costs and improve their competitiveness. He also said Lagos must assess economic progress by the improvements businesses and residents experience, rather than relying solely on economic growth figures and public spending. “The test is whether Lagos becomes more productive and more liveable,” he said. He identified electricity costs, traffic congestion, access to appropriate financing and institutional coordination as major constraints to business productivity. “A manufacturer needs reliable electricity. A worker needs a commute that does not consume productive hours. Firms need predictable approvals, appropriate finance and customers,” he said. Olusi urged the state to prioritise investment in power infrastructure serving industrial clusters, faster freight movement, streamlined business approvals, flood-resilient commercial routes and skills development. Speaking at the event, Lagos State Commissioner for Economic Planning and Budget, Mr. Ope George, said the ministry would continue to coordinate economic intelligence, development planning, budget management and performance monitoring in support of Lagos State’s long-term development aspirations. He said the 2027 economic outlook provided an opportunity to consolidate the state’s achievements, address structural challenges and strengthen its position as a competitive and resilient economy. “Our focus goes beyond economic projections. It is about shaping policies that will strengthen competitiveness, promote inclusive growth and secure a sustainable future for Lagos State,” George said. Earlier, Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Economic Planning and Budget, Mrs. Olayinka Ojo, highlighted the state’s development planning, budget monitoring and performance evaluation frameworks. She said Lagos was strengthening evidence-based governance through its long-term development plan, Medium-Term Expenditure Framework, annual budgets and regular monitoring of revenue, expenditure and project delivery. Ojo also highlighted the government’s engagement with communities and the use of platforms to improve citizens’ access to information on public projects and social intervention programmes. item.title: Customs frees 98 containers of power equipment stranded for 20 years
item.description: •Cargoes to ease pressure on substations, strengthen national grid — Tegbe By Udeme Akpan The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) has released 98 containers of electricity transmission equipment stranded at the nation’s ports, some for up to 20 years, in a move expected to strengthen the national grid and improve electricity supply across the country. The Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, disclosed this in Lagos, stating that 44 containers were released from ENL Terminal, while another 54 were cleared from APMT and Sun & Moon Terminals. He said the 98 containers represented part of more than 300 containers of transmission equipment held at the ports. The equipment, comprising high-capacity transformers, cables and switchgear, was procured to expand the transmission network, address overloaded substations and improve electricity delivery nationwide. Tegbe said: “The equipment was procured to expand the transmission network and relieve overloaded substations. Its detention stalled projects, kept existing substations under heavy strain, exposed valuable assets to deterioration and accumulated charges on the cargoes.” He noted that the prolonged detention of the equipment had imposed additional costs on businesses, households and public institutions, which continued to grapple with unreliable electricity supply. Also speaking, the Comptroller-General of Customs, Bashir Adeniyi, said the Service had commenced processes to clear the containers in collaboration with the Ministry of Power, the Nigerian Ports Authority and terminal operators. He said: “The release follows the President’s directive for immediate clearance and for agencies to resolve outstanding charges and administrative bottlenecks without delay.” Adeniyi pledged to work with the Minister until all the containers were cleared, while appealing to terminal operators to support the national effort. The Minister disclosed that an inspection of the recovered equipment showed that most of the items remained useful and viable. He said: “When evacuated, it will be verified, tested and refurbished where necessary, then deployed to project sites to complete stalled installations, relieve overloaded substations and strengthen constrained transmission corridors.” The post Customs frees 98 containers of power equipment stranded for 20 years appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: COP31 Opens As Climate, Geopolitical Pressures Mount
item.description: The UN’s annual climate talks kick off Monday in Turkey as rising temperatures heighten the urgency of action, with financial constraints and geopolitical tensions complicating efforts to secure global cooperation. More than 100,000 people are expected to attend COP31 in a sprawling expo centre in the Mediterranean seaside city of Antalya over the next two weeks. Negotiators from nearly 200 countries are facing tough discussions over how to accelerate the energy transition and provide funds to help developing nations cope with the worsening climate emergency. But observers say few major breakthroughs are expected as countries grapple with an oil price shock and geopolitical tensions fuelled by the US war with Iran and Russia’s conflict in Ukraine. The climate emergency, meanwhile, continued to wreak havoc this year as punishing heatwaves baked Europe, wildfires raged in Indonesia, and a glacier collapse triggered devastating floods in Nepal. An exceptionally strong El Niño climate phenomenon is forecast to peak later this year, adding to extreme weather and possibly helping to make 2026 or 2027 the hottest year on record. The outlook is bleak: the United Nations warned in September that global temperatures were on course to exceed 1.5C above preindustrial levels, breaching the most ambitious threshold set by the Paris Agreement. “Global leaders must pull us back from the brink and commit to rapidly transitioning away from fossil fuels and expanding renewable energy, an imperative reinforced by the current energy affordability crisis,” said Rachel Cleetus, climate programme director at the Union of Concerned Scientists. A woman walks inside the COP31 venue at the Antalya Expo Center on November 8, 2026, ahead of the opening of the UN climate conference. ‘Clean’ Electrification? Turkey is presiding over COP31, with Australia leading negotiations under an unusual arrangement that settled a dispute over who would host the conference. The partners have branded the summit as the “implementation COP”, focusing on turning commitments into concrete action after years of pledges and ambitious announcements. Turkey is promoting an “action agenda” alongside the formal negotiations that encourages countries to support non-binding pledges on issues from artificial intelligence to waste management. Its centrepiece is an “electrification” drive to raise the share of global energy demand met by electricity from around 20 percent today to 35 percent by 2035. But the initiative could become a source of friction. The European Union has called for “clean” electrification, a term that could spark debate over the role of fossil fuels in the Turkish proposal. Countries committed to transition away from fossil fuels in a landmark pact at COP28 in Dubai in 2023 but have struggled to agree on how to turn that pledge into action. item.title: 2026 Lagos Trade Fair: We’re poised to turn stability into prosperity — Tinubu
item.description: By Yinka Kolawole President Bola Tinubu has said Nigeria’s next economic priority is to translate the gains of ongoing reforms into prosperity through enterprise, industrial growth and expanded trade. Tinubu spoke at the weekend, at the opening of the 40th Lagos International Trade Fair, organised by the Lagos Chamber of Commerce and Industry (LCCI), at Tafawa Balewa Square, Lagos. The president, represented by the Minister of State for Industry, Senator John Enoh, said the Federal Government had made significant progress in stabilising the economy, adding that the focus must now shift to stimulating production, creating jobs and expanding business opportunities. “The emergency is over. The foundation has been repaired. Our task now is to turn stability into prosperity, and enterprise is at the heart of that task,” he said. Highlighting the administration’s economic achievements, Tinubu said Nigeria’s gross external reserves rose to approximately $55.07 billion in October 2026, the highest level in 18 years, while net reserves exceeded $40 billion, from less than $4 billion in 2023. He also noted that inflation declined to 14.63 per cent in September 2026, while the economy grew by 4.43 per cent in the second quarter, describing the figures as evidence of improving economic fundamentals. On trade, the President said non-oil exports exceeded $6.1 billion in 2025, while capital importation reached about $21 billion, expressing optimism that Nigerian businesses could leverage the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) to access wider markets. He, however, stressed that sustainable economic growth must be driven by domestic production and value addition rather than dependence on imports. Tinubu said the National Industrial Policy provides a roadmap for strengthening manufacturing, deepening local value chains and converting Nigeria’s raw materials into finished products. He disclosed that the Ministry of Industry, Trade and Investment and its agencies supported more than 115,000 micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in 2025, promising continued efforts to improve their access to finance, electricity and markets. He described industrial and trade policies as complementary, stressing that while industry provides goods for export, trade creates markets for locally manufactured products. The President also welcomed exhibitors from more than 20 countries and said Nigeria would host the Intra-African Trade Fair for the first time in 2027, in partnership with Afreximbank. item.title: Comedian Russell Brand To Be Sentenced For Rape, Assaults
item.description: British comedian and TV star Russell Brand, who became a household name in the 2000s as a sex-obsessed provocateur, will find out on Monday how long he will spend in jail, after he was convicted of rape and sexual assaults. Brand’s conviction last week marked the final blow in a scandal-hit showbiz career that saw him embody the anything-goes culture of 2000s British TV and radio. On Monday, he will be sentenced at London’s Southwark Crown Court, where he was told by the judge he faced a “significant custodial term” after being found guilty of one rape and three sexual assaults against four women, committed between 2004 and 2009. The maximum sentence in the UK for rape is life imprisonment. Brand, 51, who was cleared of two other alleged rapes and one count of attempted indecent assault, was remanded in custody and spent the weekend in a cell. He is facing further investigations after London’s Metropolitan Police said it was probing rape allegations by two more women. (FILES) British actor and comedian Russell Brand addresses an anti-austerity rally in Parliament Square in London on June 21, 2014. London’s Metropolitan Police on Friday said it had charged comedian and actor Russell Brand with rape and a number of other sexual offences. (Photo by Justin TALLIS / AFP) From Channel 4 to MTV and an eponymous primetime show on BBC Radio 2, the wild-haired comedian passed through major British media houses in the 2000s, where his obsession with sex contributed to his notoriety. That behaviour was also a feature of the high-profile trial, with Brand admitting that he had been “extremely promiscuous” and had used his fame to “facilitate sexual access”, although he denied the charges. He was accompanied to court most days by his wife Laura Gallacher, with whom he has three children. Calling him a “wonderful father to our children”, Gallacher told the jury that when they first dated in 2006: “It was clear it was difficult for him to be monogamous.” She said she was “very aware” of Brand’s promiscuity, as “you could read about it regularly in the papers”. British comedian and actor Russell Brand (C) leaves following a hearing at Southwark Crown Court in south London on May 30, 2025. Brand pleaded not guilty to five charges of rape and sexual assault. (Photo by HENRY NICHOLLS / AFP) ‘Shapeshifter’ Brand’s hypersexualised persona was a running joke in tabloids, with the comedian named “shagger of the year” three years in a row by The Sun newspaper from 2006-2009. “He’s a bit of a shapeshifter,” then-showbiz editor of The Sun, Gordon Smart told Channel 4. “He would present to you as he thought appropriate, quite chameleon-like.” Born to working-class parents in Essex, east of London in 1975, Brand dropped out of drama school before joining MTV at the age of 25. He was fired for turning up to work dressed as Osama bin Laden following the 9/11 terror attacks and for inviting his drug dealer into the studios. item.title: The mounting debt burden should terrify Nigerians, by Dele Sobowale
item.description: •Tinubu seeks $20.5bn; €1.04bn foreign loans to fund projects – Vanguard, October 28, 2026 •Debt worse than leprosy, Obasanjo replies Tinubu — Report, October 31, 2026 Seldom do I find myself on the same side with former President Obasanjo on matters concerning national affairs. Right now, I am on all fours with Baba Iyabo with regard to his position on President Tinubu’s request for fresh loans amounting to over $21 billion or N29.4 trillion. The debt burden is now approximately N160 trillion. Given a shamelessly rubber stamp Senate, it is a foregone conclusion that it will be approved. By December, the total debt would total N189.4 trillion. It was about N100 trillion when Buhari left the nation’s “economy on the brink of bankruptcy” – according to Tinubu. Read Also: Economy: Food warehouses now split wholesale bags as retailers battle inflation Putting the request into historical perspective would help to understand the loan request better. From 1978, under General Obasanjo, when the first $2.8 billion loan was taken, it took the country 21 years until 1999 to accumulate $36 billion or N50.4 trillion at current exchange rates. Minister of Finance, Dr Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala got us out of the debt trap in 2004. By the time President Jonathan left office in 2015, the debt had risen to $30 billion or N42 trillion once again. Eight years of Buhari’s financial mismanagement racked up N58 trillion. By the time this fresh loan is approved and taken, Tinubu would have added N89.4 trillion in just three and a half years; and, this might not be the last loan request before May 29, 2027. Whoever is President next year might be facing a debt burden well over N200 trillion. When last year I wrote that borrowing is the opium of the governing classes, it never occurred to me that the addiction could be as bad as this. Obasanjo is absolutely correct; mindless borrowing, tainted with corrupt and concealed self-interest, is indeed worse than leprosy. Lepers sometimes have children without leprosy. The malady is invariably restricted to one person and one generation. Nigeria’s debt load, made infinitely worse by Tinubu’s fiscal policy mismanagement, is already visiting diseases more virulent than leprosy on millions of Nigerians alive; and will savage millions more for at least three generations for one inescapable reason – inability to repay from revenue generation. The report which must have been glossed over by most Nigerians, when taken in conjunction with a previous one which announced that debt repayment exceeded revenue collected, should raise alarm everywhere. Despite all the attempts to mislead Nigerians, the fact is; the Federal Government, FG, is living on borrowed funds. item.title: 2027: I’ve no godfather but God — Makinde
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — The Presidential Candidate of Allied Peoples Movement, APM, Engr. Seyi Makinde, declared weekend he had no political godfather other than God, expressing confidence that divine backing and the support of Nigerians would propel him to victory in the 2027 presidential election. Read Also: ADC to APC: Test your popularity at polls, stop using courts to block us Makinde, who spoke at a church service organised by the Church of Christ in Nations, COCIN, Jos, Plateau State, yesterday, said Nigeria urgently needed a governance reset to address years of poor leadership, economic hardship and social challenges, particularly in the last three and a half years. He said the need to change the country’s direction informed his RESET NIGERIA manifesto he presented to the church leadership, describing it as a blueprint for making life easier for citizens. Makinde recalled how he defied the absence of political godfathers to become governor of Oyo State in 2019, expressing confidence that his presidential ambition would also be sustained by faith and popular support. “When I said in Oyo State in 2018 that I would like to be governor, somebody asked me, ‘Governor of which Rotary District?’ I said governor of Oyo State, and they asked, ‘with no godfather; nobody in politics who can stand in for you?’ I responded by saying, well, I have God the Father. And I became the governor of Oyo State. “This time around, we also have God the Father and that God will be merciful unto Nigeria and He will show us mercy in this country,” he said. The APM candidate said his administration in Oyo State was guided by planning, transparency and accountability, noting that he developed successive development roadmaps covering his first and second terms, from 2019 to 2027. He said the documents provided clear direction for his administration and helped ensured that promises made to the people were translated into concrete actions. Makinde said he had adopted a similar approach in preparing for the presidency, with the RESET NIGERIA agenda built around four pillars: security, the economy, education and the socio-political space. Presenting the manifesto, he challenged Nigerians to hold him accountable for the commitments contained in the document. “I want Nigerians to be able to hold me accountable, not just through promises but through documented commitments. Everything is written down in black and white, and I am prepared to be held accountable for everything contained in this document,” he said. He also urged Nigerians, particularly Christians, to participate actively in politics and prepare to exercise their democratic rights in the 2027 general election. “Please, get ready and participate. item.title: Trump Vows Comeback As Bitter Showdown With Congress Looms
item.description: Donald Trump vowed a political comeback Sunday as the major parties clashed over Democrat threats to prosecute top administration officials after the president’s Republicans lost control of Congress in midterm elections. The devastating results in last Tuesday’s vote leave Trump politically hamstrung as he enters the remaining two-year ‘lame duck’ period of his White House tenure. It also opens the door to multiple investigations by the Democrat-controlled Congress of the president, his family and senior members of his administration. On political talk shows Sunday, incoming congressional leaders from the Democratic Party promised to hold Trump and his aides to account, while the president’s top law officer resolved to defend them and Trump dug in his heels on social media. “America took a giant step back in History with the results of the last Election,” Trump said in a post on Truth Social, adding that the stock market that had grown during his tenure took a loss after the vote. “But have no fear, we will be back, BIGGER AND STRONGER THAN EVER BEFORE!” Democratic US Senate candidate James Talarico celebrates with supporters after winning the Texas race during a midterm election night watch party at the Long Center for the Performing Arts in Austin, Texas, on November 3, 2026. On Friday, Trump appointed hardline advisor Stephen Miller as his new chief of staff, signaling a bare-knuckle fightback — even though many Republicans, including Vice President JD Vance, have reflected on why they had lost so badly at the ballot box. Miller was the architect of Trump’s tough immigration policy, which analysts have identified as a contributing factor to the unpopularity of Republicans and their election debacle. Amid Democrat threats for administration officials to “lawyer up,” Trump said Saturday he was ordering the Justice Department to examine Democratic threats to impeach members of his administration, likening it to “extortion.” Supporters of Democratic US Senate candidate James Talarico cheer after he won the Texas race during a midterm election night watch party at the Long Center for the Performing Arts in Austin, Texas, on November 3, 2026. Impeaching Hegseth? With control of committees in both chambers of Congress, Democrats can summon officials, demand documents and hold public hearings, putting Trump and his senior aides under intense scrutiny. Likely subjects include the Trump family’s business and cryptocurrency dealings, government contracts involving billionaire Elon Musk, cuts to federal agencies, immigration enforcement and the conduct of the Iran war. item.title: ADC to APC: Test your popularity at polls, stop using courts to block us
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA—African Democratic Congress, ADC, has dared the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC, to test its popularity at the ballot box, rather than resort to court processes to frustrate the opposition party’s participation in the 2027 general election. Read Also: What is 25% requirement in Nigeria’s presidential election? The challenge came from the Director-General of ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Austin Akobundu, who said the massive reception accorded the party’s presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, in Sokoto State, and his running mate, Rotimi Amaechi, in Kebbi State, reflected growing public enthusiasm for the party and the desire for an alternative political direction. In a statement yesterday, Akobundu, while thanking supporters and residents who turned out to welcome the candidates, accused the federal government and APC-led administration of attempting to shut the ADC out of the political contest through what he described as a backdoor judicial process. “If the federal government and the APC believe they have the capacity to win, let them allow a free and fair election. Let Nigerians choose without intimidation, obstruction or interference. “They must stop trying to muzzle the political space, using a backdoor court process to remove us from the contest,’’ he said. On the need to protect democratic competition, Akobundu insisted that Nigerians must be free to listen to competing political ideas, attend rallies and choose their leaders without interference. “The ballot must remain the people’s choice, and every party must be allowed to campaign freely,” he said. While urging party supporters not to be distracted by the political tensions, the ADC campaign chief called for restraint and sustained grassroots mobilisation. “Let us continue to campaign peacefully and confidently, knowing that the people’s will must prevail,” he pleaded. Akobundu said ADC would continue to take its message of affordable living, opportunity and national renewal to Nigerians across the country, while expressing appreciation to those who welcomed its candidates in Sokoto and Kebbi states. item.title: Nigeria must tackle insecurity, unemployment — Obasanjo
item.description: Former President Olusegun Obasanjo has called for urgent action to address worsening insecurity, unemployment and poverty in Nigeria. Read Also: How presidential elections are won in Nigeria He also warned that leadership failures were forcing citizens to seek better opportunities abroad, often through dangerous migration routes. Obasanjo, who spoke during a panel session, themed “Lest We Forget” at the Creative Africa Nexus Weekend 2026, organised by the African Export-Import Bank in Lagos State weekend, reflected on Nigeria’s security situation since independence and said the country must confront the governance failures responsible for declining safety and economic opportunities. “We just have to do what we should do to provide job opportunities, to stem the tide of impunity, to stem the tide of poverty, to stem the tide of kidnapping and insecurity,” he said. Obasanjo recalled returning to Nigeria in 1959 after completing his military training in Britain, noting that he could travel freely across the country without fear of attacks or kidnapping. “I came back to this country after my commission as an officer in Britain in 1959. And I could go anywhere; I was posted to the north; I could go anywhere in the north, by myself alone, by day, by night,” he said. Contrasting that experience with the current security situation, he questioned how Nigeria had deteriorated to the point where citizens could no longer travel safely across several parts of the country. “Now, if you can’t do that, what has gone wrong? We have to correct what has gone wrong,” he stated. He argued that unemployment, particularly among university graduates, had become a major source of economic desperation, making it difficult to discourage young Africans from leaving their countries in search of opportunities. According to him, governments cannot continue producing graduates without creating sufficient employment opportunities and expect them to remain economically productive. Obasanjo recalled an encounter with Nigerians arrested for drug-related offences, explaining that one of the suspects had attributed his involvement in the illegal trade to the loss of legitimate employment. He said the encounter demonstrated how economic hardship could push otherwise productive individuals towards desperate decisions, although he stopped short of justifying criminal activities. Addressing irregular migration, Obasanjo said he had interacted with Africans who attempted to reach Europe through the Sahara Desert and the Mediterranean Sea, describing their experiences as distressing. “I have got those people who have attempted to cross, and the story they told me is pathetic. Some die in the Sahara, some die in the Mediterranean,” he said. item.title: Economy: Food warehouses now split wholesale bags as retailers battle inflation
item.description: By Elizabeth Adegbesan A quiet transformation is reshaping how branded food items and cooking oils move from distribution warehouses to neighborhood shops, across major wholesale food markets in Nigeria. Read Also: Can 142m Nigerian youths change 2027 elections narrative? Faced with persistent inflation, tight liquidity, and shrinking consumer purchasing power, Economy&Lifestyle findings show that bulk food warehouses are increasingly breaking down standard 50-kilogram sacks and full cartons into half-measures for small-scale retailers. Traditionally, wholesale depots in major distribution centers across the country operated on strict minimum-order volumes. Retailers were required to purchase full 50kg bags of rice, beans, or garri, full cartons of noodles, or 25-liter kegs of vegetable oil. However, as wholesale prices are consistently rising over the past two years, many corner-shop owners and market stall traders are finding it difficult to raise the capital needed to restock full units across multiple product lines. In response, warehouse operators and major distributors have adapted their inventory models, introducing official ‘half-bag’ and ‘split-carton’ wholesale tiers. Instead of turning away undercapitalised buyers, depot managers now employ dedicated staff to weigh, re-bag, and seal 25kg portions of grains and split bulk cartons of packaged foods at wholesale rates. Alhaji Musa Danjuma, a bulk grain distributor, said: “If we insist on selling only full bags, our goods will sit in the warehouse until they spoil or expire. “A retailer, who used to buy 10 full bags of local parboiled rice can barely afford three today. “By splitting bags into halves and quarters at wholesale margins, we keep our stock moving and help small traders keep their shelves stocked.” The shift has provided immediate relief for micro-retailers who form the backbone of Nigeria’s informal food distribution network. For traders operating on thin daily margins, tying up scarce capital in a single full sack of beans or sugar often meant leaving customers without other essentials like pasta, seasoning cubes, or vegetable oil. “Before now, buying one full bag of brown beans took almost all my weekly capital,” said Mrs. Ngozi Okafor, a provision store owner. “Now, the warehouse allows me to pick half a bag of beans, half a bag of rice, and half a carton of spaghetti. “My shop looks full again, and my customers do not have to walk away empty-handed because I ran out of one items.” Market analysts note that while this fractional wholesale model keeps supply chains active, it introduces minor operational costs for warehouses, including extra packaging materials, labor for re-weighing, and heightened vigilance against weight discrepancies. item.title: Election fever, Dangote Refinery to drive stock investors’ fortune at year end
item.description: By Peter Egwuatu The Nigerian stock market is projected to cross the N200 trillion market capitalisation by December 2026, while investors’ returns could exceed 57 per cent. Capital market analysts, who made the projections, said the anticipated listing of shares of Dangote Petroleum Refinery on the Nigerian Exchange Limited (NGX), coupled with improved investor confidence, strong corporate earnings, increased market liquidity and favourable macroeconomic developments, would provide further impetus for the equities market. They also projected that the NGX All-Share Index (ASI), the market’s major performance indicator, could close the year at about 280,000 points. However, some analysts have warned that profit-taking, election-related uncertainties and global economic developments could trigger intermittent volatility. But the analysts agreed that the concern over 2027 general election is around possible policy change adding that if there are no major adverse economic policy developments capable of undermining investor confidence the impact of the election would be less severe. Market performance so far A review of the market’s performance Year-to-Date, YtD, as at last week, showed that investors’ wealth had increased by N62.76 trillion, representing a 60.47 per cent appreciation. Market capitalisation, which measures the total value of listed equities, rose from N99.376 trillion at the beginning of the year to N162.134 trillion last week. Similarly, the NGX ASI appreciated by 60.5 per cent, rising from 155,613.03 points at the beginning of the year to 249,710.59 points. The impressive performance has been supported by relative stability in the foreign exchange market, renewed investor confidence, strong corporate earnings, easing inflation, improved liquidity in the financial system and the decision of the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) of the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) to reduce the Monetary Policy Rate (MPR) to 23 per cent. Analysts’ projections Speaking to Financial Vanguard on his projection for the year-end, Olatunde Amolegbe, immediate past President, Chartered Institute of Stockbrokers (CIS), and Managing Director, Arthur Stevens Asset Management Limited, said he remained cautiously optimistic about the equities market. He stated: “I remain cautiously optimistic about the Nigerian stock market for the rest of the year. My expectation is that the All-Share Index will deliver a full-year return of approximately 57.65%. “Although the market has recorded impressive gains so far, I expect some moderation in the coming weeks, as investors may take profits following the significant rally we have witnessed. We could also see some volatility as investors reposition their portfolios ahead of the new year. “On the positive side, relatively strong corporate earnings, improved investor confidence, increased domestic participation and ongoing economic reforms should continue to provide support for the market. item.description: By Efe Onodjae LAGOS — THE Lagos State governorship candidates of the All Progressives Congress, APC, Dr Obafemi Hamzat; African Democratic Congress, ADC, Mr Gbadebo Rhodes-Vivour; Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Mr Funso Doherty and Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, Mr Adedeji Doherty, yesterday, unveiled their development plans for housing, traffic congestion, transportation, security and infrastructure if elected in 2027. Read Also: Explainer: What INEC’s 2023 results in Lagos, Oyo, Osun actually reveal They presented their credentials, policy proposals and vision for the state ahead of the governorship election. The candidates spoke at a debate organised by the Nigeria Debate Consortium, which comprises Vanguard Newspaper, Channels Television, TVC News, Punch Newspaper and The Cable. During the debate, the candidates outlined different approaches to addressing the developmental challenges facing Lagos. On the developmental challenges facing the state, the APC candidate, Dr Hamzat, emphasised continuity and expansion of existing infrastructure, while the ADC candidate, Mr Rhodes-Vivour, called for a departure from what he described as two decades of bad governance. In his remarks, the NDC candidate, Mr Doherty, questioned the political interests surrounding the state’s public transportation system, alleging that the failure to modernise the sector was deliberate. Taming traffic in Lagos On traffic congestion, Doherty alleged that the persistent gridlock in Lagos was being sustained by vested interests benefiting from the existing chaotic public transportation system. He argued that the state’s traffic problems were not simply the result of inadequate infrastructure but also reflected poor management of existing roads and the failure to modernise public transportation. The NDC candidate also alluded to the informal transport network popularly associated with agberos, arguing that the interests surrounding the system had made its modernisation politically difficult. He said: “Lagos continues to rely on dilapidated commercial buses operating chaotically, contributing to gridlock and making commuting difficult for residents. “Our public transportation system is not modernised. Thousands of rickety buses are moving around. We must ask ourselves: are these what our people deserve? Why has it taken so long to modernise public transportation? “In my opinion, the lack of modern transportation is not by accident. There are vested interests in operating the bus system the way it is. Many of us understand the agbero system; there is an ecosystem around it, and there is no political will to deal with that problem.” “We would modernise public transportation because we would be elected by the people and not by the agbero network,” he added. item.title: INEC in Eye of the Storm: Electoral body battles to clean voters’ register – Investigation
item.description: By Jide Ajani There is perhaps no greater threat to electoral integrity than an unreliable Voters’ Register. Before the first ballot is cast or the first result announced, the credibility of an election is already being determined by the document that establishes who is entitled to vote. Read Also: * Explainer: Who won 2023 presidential 2023 in Kaduna, Katsina – the 161,829 votes difference * Explainer: What INEC’s 2023 results in Lagos, Oyo, Osun actually reveal The Voters’ Register is the foundation of the electoral process. It defines the electorate, determines the numerical strength of constituencies and provides the basis for accreditation and voting. It is, fundamentally, the official record of a people’s democratic membership. Yet, in Nigeria, its credibility remains a persistent source of anxiety. The historical paradox: have we really progressed? Nigeria has travelled a considerable distance from the largely manual registration arrangements of the 1950s to biometric registration, electronic databases and the deployment of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS). The 1959 general election, conducted under the Electoral Commission of Nigeria (ECN), had approximately nine million registered voters. Subsequent elections in 1964/65, 1979, 1983 and 1993 exposed different administrative and political challenges associated with voter registration. 4th Republic The Fourth Republic introduced more sophisticated systems, including permanent voter cards, biometric identification and mechanisms for detecting duplicate registrations. Yet technological advancement has not necessarily translated into greater electoral credibility. A bigger register is not automatically a better register. A digital register is not necessarily reliable, and biometric technology is not beyond manipulation. Consider the fluctuations in registration figures: 73.5 million in 2011, 67.4 million in 2015 and approximately 84 million in 2019. Such changes do not establish manipulation, since legitimate deletions and corrections occur The real test is fidelity: whether the names represent living, eligible citizens entitled to vote, or whether they are mere AI-generated entities. INEC and the collapse of public confidence An electoral commission’s credibility rests not merely on constitutional independence but on demonstrable impartiality, competence and transparency. Constitutional independence in itself does not guarantee operational independence when the personnel saddled with responsibilities decide to go rogue on the system. When public confidence in INEC declines, virtually every administrative decision becomes vulnerable to suspicion, from voter registration and PVC distribution to accreditation and results management. This is the distinction between administrative validity and democratic legitimacy. item.title: Bandits burn 12 family members
item.description: Twelve members of the same family have been killed after armed bandits set their residence ablaze during an attack on Gidan Taba village in Maradun Local Government Area of Zamfara State. Seven other residents were also abducted during the attack, which occurred on Saturday night in Dosara Birnin Kaya Ward, despite efforts by the community to alert security agencies. This is coming barely one week after bandits ambushed security personnel at Gidan Kano along the Gusau-Sokoto highway within the same local government and killed five policemen. A resident, who spoke to Daily Trust on condition of anonymity, said the attackers invaded the residence of one Mallam Muhammadu Sani at about 10 pm. 1 killed in NDC rally as attacks rise Middle Belt leaders’ visit to Tinubu raises unity questions He said 13 members of the family were trapped inside a room after locking themselves in to escape being abducted by the attackers. According to him, those inside the room included Sani, his two wives and their six children, as well as the wife of his younger brother and their three children. He said the bandits ordered the occupants to open the door, but when they refused, the attackers set the room ablaze. Only the wife of Sani’s younger brother reportedly escaped, while the remaining 12 occupants died from the intense heat and fire. The resident said the community immediately contacted the Maradun Local Government Chairman, Sanusi Ahmed Dosara, who made efforts to reach security formations for assistance. However, he said the security agencies could not intervene before the tragedy occurred. “We informed the local government chairman, Dosara, and he tried all he could to reach the security personnel. He told us he had spoken with different security formations, but nobody came to our rescue,” he said. He expressed disappointment that no security personnel responded to their distress calls despite the village’s proximity to Maradun town, where military and police formations are located. “Imagine, the distance between our village and Dosara is just about half a kilometre, while from Dosara to Maradun is about one kilometre. In total, it is just about one and a half kilometres between our village and the local government headquarters. “There is a military base in Maradun, a mobile police base and a police headquarters, yet none of them came to our aid until the bandits burnt the 12 people alive,” he said. Another resident confirmed that seven other people were abducted during the attack and remained in the custody of the bandits as of the time he spoke to Daily Trust. He appealed to security agencies to strengthen their presence in the area and take urgent measures to protect residents against further attacks. item.title: Zuba fruit market traders decry poor access road
item.description: Some traders at Zuba Fruit Market, Federal Capital Territory (FCT), have decried the poor access road, saying it disrupts business activities, discourages customers and increases transportation costs. They spoke in separate interviews with the News Agency of Nigeria on Wednesday in Abuja. They said the road, which had deteriorated over time, becomes almost impassable during the rainy season due to deep potholes, muddy sections and poor drainage. According to them, the poor condition of the road discourages customers from visiting the market and causes delays in transporting fresh fruits and vegetables. A fruit wholesaler, Mr Mohammed Usman, said many commercial vehicles avoided the road because of its poor state, forcing traders to pay higher transport fares. “The bad road has affected our business seriously. Many transporters charge extra because they fear damage to their vehicles. “Some customers also turn back when they see the condition of the road, while others prefer buying from markets with easier access,” he said. Another trader, Mr Augustine Igwe, said vehicles conveying fruits from farms frequently developed mechanical faults due to the poor condition of the road. One of the bad roads in Zuba “We spend more money repairing our vehicles and paying higher transport fares. These costs eventually increase the prices of fruits. “Sometimes, vehicles carrying fruits get stuck, leading to delays and spoilage of some produce. The extra cost is eventually passed on to buyers,” he said. A buyer, Mrs Esther Okoli, described the road as a major challenge, especially for elderly people and parents visiting the market with children. “The road is in a terrible state. Many customers complain before coming here, while transporters charge us more because of the bad road. “Whenever it rains, the road becomes almost impassable because of stagnant water and deep potholes. Carrying goods through such conditions is stressful,” she said. Another buyer, Mr Emmanuel Johnson, said the poor condition of the road increased the cost and difficulty of moving goods from the market. “I shop here for affordable prices, but the poor road discourages buyers. Commercial vehicles often avoid the market, forcing us to carry purchases over long distances. ”A commercial driver, Mr Abdullahi Ibrahim, said frequent use of the road increased vehicle maintenance costs due to damaged tyres and suspension systems. He appealed to the FCT Administration to prioritise the rehabilitation of the access road to improve transportation and support businesses operating in the market. NAN reports that Zuba Fruit Market supplies fruits and vegetables daily, serving thousands of consumers within the FCT and neighbouring communities. The traders and buyers expressed optimism that prompt government intervention would improve access to the market, reduce transportation costs and enhance economic activities in the area.(NAN)

item.title: 2027 elections: Stop the violence!
item.description: The 2027 general elections are a couple of months away, but the campaigns are already taking a dangerous turn. Barely weeks after political parties commenced electioneering, Nigeria is witnessing an alarming wave of violence, killing, intimidation, and destruction of campaign materials. This is a disturbing portent of what could happen if decisive action is not taken. The killing of Ifeanyi Nwolie, a 43-year-old supporter of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), during the violent disruption of activities surrounding the party’s governorship campaign in Enugu is particularly tragic. Suspected political thugs reportedly attacked supporters at the Akanu Ibiam International Airport and later around the party secretariat. Nwolie sustained gunshot injuries and subsequently died. His death has become another grim statistic in Nigeria’s history of political violence. Equally reprehensible was the attack on Peter Obi’s convoy in Calabar, Cross River State, by suspected hoodlums armed with machetes and sticks. Windscreens were smashed as the presidential candidate returned from a visit to the Obong of Calabar. The police subsequently announced the arrest of a suspect, Victor Edet. There was also a potentially explosive confrontation between NDC and APC supporters in the city, which security operatives managed to prevent. Meanwhile, APC campaign billboards and posters have reportedly been vandalised in Kano and other Northern cities by irate youths. APC supporters travelling to a campaign rally in Katsina were also attacked, leaving a female passenger injured. The police arrested 14 suspects, including a minor. Other reported disruptions of political activities, including Governor Alex Otti’s campaign inauguration in Abia, reinforce the need for vigilance. The Nigerian Police Force has responded by reading the riot act. Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, directed Commissioners nationwide to prevent the destruction of campaign materials, intimidation and harassment. The police warned that offenders, including those sponsoring or financing such criminal activities, would be arrested and prosecuted. These are welcome assurances, but Nigerians expect action, not mere warnings. The implications are grave. Campaign violence suppresses participation, deepens political divisions and encourages retaliation. Most frightening is the possibility of a major presidential or governorship candidate being killed or seriously injured. Such an incident could trigger widespread unrest, communal reprisals and a national crisis. This must be prevented at all costs. Candidates must demonstrate leadership and patriotism. They should restrain their supporters, avoid inflammatory rhetoric, respect opponents’ rights to campaign and condemn violence without equivocation. Security agencies must investigate impartially, arrest perpetrators, prosecute their sponsors, irrespective of political affiliation and stay above board. item.title: Indicted judge who sits in judgement can only deliver injustice, by Owei Lakemfa
item.description: Ten weeks before the contentious and increasingly violent general elections in the country, Justice Peter Odo Lifu of the Federal High Court Abuja nullified the leadership of one of the two main opposition parties, the African Democratic Congress, ADC. He did not only purport to remove the David Mark-Rauf Aregbesola leadership of the party, but also nullified the nomination of all the party’s candidates in the elections. This includes that of its Presidential candidate, former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar. The Lifu judgement was made a day after the party launched its presidential campaigns in Sokoto. On the day of the judgement, the ADC Presidential train had moved to Kebbi State where it was attacked by thugs. This attack was not surprising. In fact, the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC Presidential train of Peter Obi holds the record of suffering the most attacks in the country. In broad day light with cameras rolling, it has been attacked by thugs in Edo, Benue, Cross Rivers, and most recently, Delta State. The most recent attack on the African Action Congress, AAC Presidential team was perhaps the most graphic and documented. It was an attack in a restaurant in Ado Ekiti carried out by clearly identifiable criminals captured in various video recordings and CCTV camera. The ruling All Progressives Congress, APC has also recorded attacks. An APC campaign convoy headed for a rally in Funtua, Katsina State was attacked on the Yashi-Funtua road resulting in fourteen arrests. In the same state, two APC supporters were reportedly killed in Yankara while heading for a pro-Governor Dikko Radda rally. In Zaria, Kaduna State, APC campaign vehicles were reportedly attacked in September, 2026. Woven into this rising political violence are the continued attacks by terrorists and bandits across the country. All these are ominous signs of what 2027 might hold for the country, only for Justice Lifu, a judge indicted on Tuesday, June 16, 2026 by the Court of Appeal, to return to his judicial rascality and, attempt on Thursday, November 5, 2026 to set the political system on fire. Lifu had on June 15, 2026 deregistered the ADC and four other political parties. What irked the Appeal Court was that twenty four days earlier, it had ordered a stay of proceedings in the suit and, this had been brought to the attention of Lifu in open court. But the High Court judge willfully decided to override the decision of the higher court and, in fact, sat on appeal over it. It seemed nothing mattered to Lifu including the facts of the case before him. Clearly, whatever gains he hoped to get, outweighed the consequences he thought he could suffer by his judicial recklessness. A clearly angry Court of Appeal, reversed Lifu’s judgment describing it as a: “brazen violation of the hierarchy of the court and the 1999 Constitution”. item.title: Will the election hold? By Suleiman A. Suleiman
item.description: Will the 2027 general elections hold as currently scheduled? There are compelling legal, logistical, and contingency reasons to doubt that the elections will hold as presently scheduled for January 16 and February 6, 2027, for the federal and state elections, respectively. First, the entire election is already in a legal peril. According to an INEC press release dated 26th October, 2026, the Commission claims to have conducted a physical display of what it calls “preliminary” Register of Voters at registration areas nationwide from 9th to 15th October, and published this “preliminary” copy online on 26th October. INEC then added that: “Meanwhile, the commission continues to process claims and objections arising from the exercise in accordance with the Electoral Act, 2026, preparatory to the certification and publication of the final register of voters on 15th December 2026”. There are a thousand and one legal problems with this release because nearly everything INEC says in this release is not only a direct violation of the Electoral Act 2026, but puts the entire election into a legal peril. By publishing the preliminary voter’s register on 26th October, and promising to release the certified copy of the register on 15th December, INEC has already breached the law, twice. The wording of Section 9(6) of the Electoral Act 2026 could not be clearer, as it says: “The registration of voters, updating and revision of the Register of Voters under this section shall stop not later than 90 days before any election covered by this Act”. Moreover, Section 19(1) of the Act further provides that: “Subject to the provisions of section 9 (6) of this Act, the Commission shall, not later than 90 days to a general election, appoint a period of seven days during which a copy of the voters’ register for each Local Government, Area Council or Ward shall be displayed or published for public scrutiny at every registration area and on its official website or any website established by the Commission for that purpose”. One does not need to be a lawyer to grasp the legal force of these provisions. First, these are legal provisions, not mere administrative timelines that INEC or anyone can bend or ignore at will. The provisions require INEC to ensure that continuous voter registration, publication, claims and objections, and revisions and clean-up of the Voter Register “shall stop not later than 90 days before any election covered by this Act”. That deadline is 18 October, 2026 and cannot be extended or changed unless the law is amended. In other words, the Electoral Act requires INEC to have a final copy of the register of Voters latest by 18th October, 2026 for the opening presidential and national assembly elections on January 16, 2027. INEC does not have the final Voter register, and in its own words, it would not have it until 32 days before the election on 15th December, 2026. That is in clear violation of the Electoral Act. item.title: Beyond the Promise of AI: Putting patients at the heart of healthcare in Nigeria
item.description: By PAVEL URSU For a pregnant woman in a rural settlement in Kuje, Abuja, accessing specialist care may mean hours of travel, considerable expense, and uncertainty. For a child in a hard-to-reach community in Borno State, pneumonia may go undetected because a health worker lacks the necessary diagnostic tools. In a riverine community in Bayelsa State, a person with tuberculosis (TB) may face delays in diagnosis because radiology services are difficult to access. These scenarios reflect a fundamental challenge facing Nigeria’s healthcare system: those who need timely medical attention most often face the greatest barriers to receiving it. Again, consider a scenario in which a frontline health worker is equipped with an artificial intelligence (AI)-powered tool that facilitates early identification of complications, interpretation of medical images, or recognition of patients requiring urgent referrals. As African countries explore AI-enabled healthcare, a critical question emerges: is technology being adopted solely due to its availability, or because it demonstrably improves health outcomes? To be sure, the value of AI lies not in its sophistication, but in its ability to improve health outcomes, expand access to appropriate care and reduce inequalities. AI offers opportunities to strengthen healthcare delivery, particularly where specialists, diagnostic equipment and other resources are limited. When properly validated and implemented, it can help health workers identify risks, interpret clinical information and make informed decisions. Tuberculosis screening illustrates this potential. AI-powered computer-aided detection (CAD) tools analyze chest X-rays to identify abnormalities suggestive of tuberculosis, helping health workers prioritize individuals for further testing. For eligible populations aged 15 years and older, these tools can improve screening and triage, particularly in settings with limited access to radiologists. However, screening must be followed by confirmatory testing, clinical assessment and timely linkage to treatment. Nigeria offers encouraging evidence of this potential. A study involving 869 participants across 17 communities in the Federal Capital Territory evaluated an AI-enabled automated microscope for detecting Schistosoma haematobium ) eggs in urine, an indicator of urinary schistosomiasis. Compared with conventional microscopy, the tool demonstrated approximately 89 per cent sensitivity and 99 per cent specificity. Although promising, these findings require further validation in routine clinical settings. Affordability, reliability, quality assurance and scalability will determine whether such innovations can deliver sustained benefits. Put differently, success should be measured not only by AI’s ability to detect disease, but by whether patients receive appropriate care as a result. item.title: Sim-swap fraud now in vogue
item.description: By Owolola Adebola We are in a period when a smartphone functions as a digital wallet, identity card, and security key all at once. One of the oldest tricks in the cybercrime playbook has returned with a vengeance. SIM-swap fraud is at it. It is also known as SIM swapping, SIM hijacking, or phone-number takeover. Yes, it has surged in popularity among criminals worldwide. Once considered a niche tactic targeting high-value crypto holders, it is now a mainstream method of account takeover, capable of emptying bank accounts, draining mobile-money wallets, and locking victims out of their digital lives in minutes. Recent data from the United Kingdom, Africa, and elsewhere show dramatic increases, while even in the United States, where reported cases have declined, the technique remains a high-leverage attack that continues to evolve with artificial intelligence and eSIM technology. One may ask what exactly SIM-swap fraud is. A SIM swap occurs when a criminal convinces a mobile network operator to transfer a victim’s phone number from the legitimate SIM (or eSIM) to a card or profile the attacker controls. Once the transfer is complete, the victim’s phone loses service. The phone would often show “No Service” or no signal, while all calls, text messages, and one-time passcodes (OTPs) route to the criminal’s device. Because so many services still rely on SMS-based two-factor authentication or password resets sent by text, the attacker can then reset passwords for email, banking, social media, and cryptocurrency accounts with relative ease. The process typically unfolds in stages. First comes reconnaissance: criminals harvest personal details, which include name, date of birth, address, account numbers, or recent transactions, all from data breaches, phishing, social media over sharing, or dark-web marketplaces. Armed with this information, they contact the carrier, often claiming the phone was lost or damaged, and request a replacement SIM. In some cases, they bribe an insider or walk into a retail store with forged documents. With eSIM technology, the transfer can happen remotely without any physical card changing hands. Once control is established, the attacker intercepts OTPs, seizes accounts, and moves funds, frequently within minutes of the swap. In a way, several factors have made SIM swapping newly attractive. The sheer volume of personal data available online has lowered the barrier to entry. Dark-web services now advertise complete SIM-swap packages starting as low as a few hundred dollars, sometimes bundled with stolen identity information. Reliance on SMS as a second factor of authentication remains widespread; many banks, exchanges, and platforms still treat a texted code as sufficient proof of identity. The rise of mobile money in Africa and elsewhere has created especially rich targets, because wallets are often tied directly to a phone number. item.title: 2027: APC chieftain laments 73% voter apathy in Aramoko
item.description: By Rotimi Ojomoyela ADO-EKITI — A chieftain of the All Progressives Congress (APC) and member of the President Bola Tinubu/APC 2027 Presidential Campaign Council, Engineer Atinuke Owolabi, has expressed concern over the low voter turnout in Aramoko-Ekiti during the 2023 presidential election, saying about 73 per cent of registered voters in the community did not participate. Owolabi, who is also the convener of PBAT-MOB Aramoko Community Engagement, spoke during an APC voter education exercise and community engagement in Aramoko, Ekiti Central Senatorial District, over the weekend. The programme, organised in support of the re-election bids of President Tinubu and Senate Leader, Senator Michael Opeyemi Bamidele, was held under the theme, “My Vote, My Voice”. She also represents the South-West as a member of the North Central Development Commission. Owolabi said voter education was essential to strengthening democracy, particularly in rural communities where inadequate information about electoral procedures could discourage participation or lead to invalid votes. Presenting figures from the 2023 presidential election, she said Ekiti State had 988,923 registered voters, out of whom 315,058 were accredited, while 308,171 valid votes were recorded and 6,301 ballots were rejected. She said available ward-level records for Aramoko I and Aramoko II showed a combined 17,426 registered voters, compared with 4,680 votes reportedly cast during the presidential election. According to her, the figures indicated that approximately 12,746 registered voters did not participate, representing about 73 per cent of the electorate in the two wards. She urged residents to improve their participation in future elections, stressing the need for the community to translate its voting strength into meaningful democratic engagement. Owolabi said the exercise was designed to educate residents on voting procedures, encourage participation and reduce the number of rejected ballots. The programme also featured the unveiling of a voter education handbook intended to guide residents on electoral processes, identification of polling units and the proper use of their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs). She said: “I believe voter education is key. If we cannot completely eliminate rejected votes, we should at least be able to reduce them in Ekiti State, particularly in Aramoko, my community. “We are here to sensitise our people on the correct way to vote. When they go to the polling units, they must ensure that they vote correctly. “We have the population, and we have the voters. What is really lacking is adequate information. Our people need to understand the right way to vote. “Today, we have unveiled a voter education handbook, which is a welcome development. Through this handbook, our people will be taught what elections are all about. item.title: 2027 Elections: Lagos APC Candidate Hamzat Promises 4,000 CNG Buses, 77 Electric Ferries
item.description: The Lagos State governorship candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Obafemi Hamzat, has promised to deploy 4,000 compressed natural gas (CNG) buses to move one million passengers daily as part of plans to ease transportation challenges in the state. Hamzat, the incumbent Deputy Governor, also disclosed plans to expand water transportation with 77 electric ferries and improve connectivity between different parts of Lagos through an integrated transport system. ﻿ He made the promises on Sunday during the Lagos governorship debate organised by the Nigeria Debate Consortium, comprising Channels Television, TVC News, Punch Newspaper, The Cable, and Vanguard Newspaper. Explaining his transportation plans, Hamzat said the objective was to reduce commuting time and give residents more opportunities to rest and spend time with their families. “The plan is to give back time to the citizens to plan, to rest, to spend with their family. There’s nowhere in Africa that the private sector has funded a rail. “Since BRT started, it has done 77 million journeys; that is with 1,000 buses. My plan says we will push it to 4,000 buses; the idea is to move one million people a day with 4,000 CNG buses, meaning up to 5,000, create BRt lane from Marina to Epe, from Marina to Badagry and so on and so forth,” he said. “Today, over four million people have the Cowry card. What does that mean? It means you can use ferry, you can use rail, and you can use BRT buses — one payment — so that we can deal with how to subsidise it. On healthcare, the APC candidate promised to expand access to medical services by increasing the number of primary healthcare centres providing round-the-clock services. Hamzat said that out of the over 300 primary healthcare centres, the government planned to increase its flagship PHCs from 87 to 150, with the facilities operating 24 hours a day. He also disclosed that the state government was building more hospitals to improve healthcare access for residents. item.title: No Political Will To Deal With Agberos In Lagos, Says NDC’s Funsho Doherty
item.description: The governorship candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Lagos State, Funsho Doherty, has blamed the persistence of the agbero system in the state on a lack of political will by successive administrations to reform the transport sector. Agberos are transport touts who collect money from commercial bus drivers and other transport operators at motor parks, bus stops and along roads, often claiming to represent transport unions or park authorities. Speaking during the Lagos Governorship Debate on Sunday, Doherty said powerful interests within the existing transport system had made it difficult for successive governments to tackle the activities of the operators. The debate was organised by the Nigeria Debate Consortium, a coalition of five media organisations: Channels Television, TVC News, The PUNCH, TheCable and Vanguard Newspapers. “Many of us understand this notion of the agbero system that people talk about. There is no political will to deal with that problem,” Doherty said. He argued that meaningful reform of public transportation would require a government that was accountable to residents rather than interests benefiting from the existing arrangement. “We will modernise the transportation system because we will be elected by the people, not by an agbero network,” he said. item.title: Lagos 2027: PDP’s Deji Doherty Defends Alliance With Wike, Tinubu
item.description: The governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Lagos State, Adedeji Doherty, has defended his political relationship with the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, despite the latter’s support for President Bola Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress (APC). Doherty said Wike’s position in the APC-led Federal Government does not make him an enemy of democracy, arguing that politics and democracy can accommodate different political alignments. He spoke during the 2027 Lagos State governorship debate organised by Channels Television, TVC, Punch Newspapers, Vanguard Newspapers and The Cable on Sunday. Responding to a question on how he could offer a genuine opposition alternative in Lagos despite emerging from a PDP faction loyal to Wike, Doherty said his candidacy was the product of 26 years of political work and grassroots support. “My emergence in the People’s Democratic Party is out of 26 years of hard work, consistency, determination, and continued support for the grassroots. I have built a grassroots structure right from scratch, and I know there are a lot of people here that can testify to that. That’s number one. “Number two is that Nyesom Wike is our leader. He’s our national leader. He will continue to be my leader, and he will continue to show us that politics and democracy are not enemies,” he said. The PDP candidate further defended Wike’s relationship with the President, pointing to what he described as benefits from the Federal Government. “Once we are getting results from the FCT, we are getting results from Mr. President, we are getting monies into the pockets of governors in different states,” Doherty added. item.title: [VIDEO] Lagos Candidates Disagree On Flooding, Traffic, Housing, Education At Governorship Debate
item.description: Four candidates contesting the 2027 Lagos State governorship election have presented different approaches to tackling the state’s challenges of flooding, traffic congestion, housing, and education, with promises ranging from technology-driven environmental solutions and expanded public transportation to affordable homes and free education. ﻿ The candidates — Gbadebo Rhodes-Vivour of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Obafemi Hamzat of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Funso Doherty of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), and Deji Doherty of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) — made their positions known on Sunday at a governorship debate organised by the Nigeria Debate Consortium in Lagos. The debate featured competing assessments of the state’s development priorities, with the opposition candidates criticising aspects of the APC government’s record and Hamzat defending its policies while outlining plans to expand infrastructure and social services. Flooding: Technology, Drainage, Environmental Management On flooding, Rhodes-Vivour blamed what he described as decades of bad governance for some of the challenges confronting Lagos residents, promising a technology-driven approach to environmental management if elected. Gbadebo Rhodes-Vivour is the ADC governorship candidate for the 2027 general elections.
